subject.title: Memory MVP: add review, edit, forget, and conflict-resolution flows

question: What memory lifecycle contract should OpenClaw support for review, edit, forget, tombstone/supersede, and conflict resolution across active memory plugins?
rationale: The gap is real, but the durable storage model, privacy and deletion semantics, rollback behavior, review UX, and plugin SDK boundary are product/API choices automation should not choose.

options.title: Define shared lifecycle contract first
options.body: Keep this as the broad design tracker, settle schema and plugin API semantics, then split implementation into schema, provenance, write-path, and operator-surface PRs.

options.title: Scope v1 to memory-core
options.body: Implement the lifecycle only for the bundled memory-core backend first, accepting a later compatibility step for other memory plugins.

options.title: Defer active-memory lifecycle work
options.body: Rely on Memory Wiki and LanceDB experiments for now while concrete stale-memory bugs remain tracked separately.

recommendation.title: Define shared lifecycle contract first
recommendation.body: Keep this as the broad design tracker, settle schema and plugin API semantics, then split implementation into schema, provenance, write-path, and operator-surface PRs.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent memory schema, SDK, and Memory Wiki history makes this the best available routing candidate for lifecycle contract direction.
